title: PS5 Pro for GTA 6, or Save It for a PC Graphics Card? How I'd Decide
summary: GTA 6 lands on PS5 and Xbox on November 19. Here's how I'd choose between a PS5 Pro now and a PC graphics card upgrade for later.
body_markdown:
GTA 6 arrives on November 19, and Rockstar moved digital pre-loading up to November 10. That puts a very specific question in front of a lot of people who play on both a console and a PC: do I buy a PS5 Pro now, or do I put that money into a graphics card and wait for the PC version that nobody has dated yet?


I keep landing on the same answer, but it depends on one thing more than any spec: where you actually want to play this game in the next twelve months.


## The two contenders


On one side is the[PlayStation 5 Pro](https://www.newegg.com/p/9SIAN2HKUK0984?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) . GTA 6 is listed on the PlayStation Store as PS5 Pro Enhanced. What Rockstar hasn't done, as of early November, is publish a clear breakdown of what that enhancement means in frame rate or resolution terms. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson has hinted that the console versions target 30fps, and leaks have pointed to a performance mode, but I wouldn't buy a console based on a leak.


On the other side is a GPU upgrade for a PC you already own. Rockstar has announced only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S versions. Any PC date you read is a report, not an announcement, and Rockstar's history says a PC port comes later rather than sooner.

## Deep dive: when the PS5 Pro makes sense


If you don't own a PS5 or Xbox at all, the decision is mostly made for you. A graphics card can't run a game that isn't on PC, and I don't think it's reasonable to wait a year or more for something you're excited about now.


The Pro's 2TB SSD also matters more than usual here. Rockstar's pre-load update put GTA 6 at 212GB, which is a big chunk of a standard console. The Pro's Newegg listing shows 2TB of storage, Wi-Fi 7 and one HDMI 2.1 port, so you're less likely to spend launch night deleting other games.


If the Pro is more console than you want, the[PS5 Digital Slim](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16868110357?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) plays the same game. You lose whatever the Pro enhancement turns out to be, plus storage headroom, since the listing shows 825GB. One practical note: neither of these has a disc drive, so if you were planning to buy GTA 6 on disc, check how your copy is delivered before you decide.


## Deep dive: when I'd buy a graphics card instead


If you already own a base PS5, I'd be much slower to buy a Pro just for one game whose Pro mode hasn't been described yet. I'd play on the console I have and see what the Pro actually changes once people can compare them side by side.


Meanwhile, a GPU upgrade pays off right away in every PC game you already play. My rule is to buy for the games you already play and treat a future GTA 6 port as a bonus. Here's what I'd look at.


The[GIGABYTE Eagle RTX 5070 Ti](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932769?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) is the card I'd point most people toward if they game at 1440p or 4K. Its listing shows 16GB of GDDR7 on a 256-bit bus, which is the memory headroom I want for big open-world games that haven't shipped on PC yet.


On the AMD side, the[SAPPHIRE PULSE RX 9070 XT](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814202450?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) also has 16GB on a 256-bit bus. The listing shows a 304W board power and a 750W recommended power supply, so check your PSU before you order.


If you want 16GB without a big power draw, look at the[MSI RTX 5060 Ti 16G Gaming Trio OC](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814137954?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) or the[GIGABYTE RX 9060 XT 16GB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932806?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) . Both use a 128-bit bus, so they're 1080p and lighter-1440p cards, but the 16GB buffer keeps them useful longer than 8GB versions. The[GIGABYTE AERO RTX 5070](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16814932773?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) sits between those tiers with 12GB, which is fine for current games; I'd just be more cautious about 12GB for games that don't exist on PC yet.


If you game on a PC monitor and want one screen that works for both, something like the[MSI MAG 272URDF E16](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16824475488?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_ps5-pro-or-pc-graphics-card-gta-6) has two HDMI 2.1 ports and a 4K 160Hz mode, so a console and a PC can both stay plugged in.


## Who wins, by situation


- **No current console:** PS5 Pro, or the Digital Slim if you don't care about the Pro extras. You want to play on the 19th.
- **Base PS5 owner:** keep it, play on day one, and decide on the Pro once its GTA 6 mode is documented.
- **PC-only player who'll wait:** upgrade the GPU for the games you play now, aim for 16GB, and don't pay extra just for a port that hasn't been announced.
- **Older PC and no console:** the console is the cheaper path to GTA 6 itself, and the GPU can wait until the PC version is real.


The one thing I wouldn't do is buy a high-end graphics card specifically for GTA 6 before a PC version is even announced. By the time a PC version exists, you'll know its real requirements, and you might be shopping in a different market.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is GTA 6 coming to PC?** Rockstar has only announced PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S versions for the November 19, 2026 launch. A PC release has not been announced, so any PC timing you see is a report, not a date.


**Does GTA 6 have PS5 Pro enhancements?** The PlayStation Store lists GTA 6 as PS5 Pro Enhanced. As of early November 2026, Rockstar had not published a detailed breakdown of what the Pro version changes, such as frame rate targets or resolution modes.


**Does the PS5 Pro have a disc drive?** No. The PS5 Pro ships without a disc drive and with a 2TB SSD. If you buy games on disc, you need the separate disc drive add-on.


**When can I pre-load GTA 6?** Rockstar moved digital pre-loading up to November 10, 2026. On PS5 it starts at midnight local time; on Xbox it starts at 12 a.m. GMT worldwide.


**Which graphics card would I buy now for a future GTA 6 PC port?** I would not buy a card for a game with no PC date. If your current card is already struggling, a 16GB card such as an RTX 5070 Ti or RX 9070 XT is the safer long-term buy than an 8GB or 12GB model.
